bugs.name: Saving a user's repository limit as 0 resets it to -1
bugs.summary: The report says that in Site Administration > Edit User Account, saving Maximum Number of Repositories as 0 makes the form show -1 when reopened.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that a saved limit of 0 is shown as 0 when the form is reopened.
bugs.actual: After updating a user with a maximum repository count of 0, reopening the edit form was reported to show -1.
reproSteps: In Site Administration, edit a user account.
Set Maximum Number of Repositories to 0 and update the account.
Reopen the edit form and check the value.
bugs.reason: Not reproduced: saving 0 keeps 0. Across repeated attempts on a new user and a seeded user, typed and entered by keyboard, the request sent max_repo_creation=0 and the reopened form showed 0 every time; the server passes 0 through unchanged.

bugs.name: Monitoring Trace opens an empty diagnostic list
bugs.summary: The report claims that Site Administration > Monitoring > Trace shows only the Goroutines count header with a blank list below it, as if the diagnostic list failed to load.
bugs.expected: The reporter expects the Trace page to list goroutines or processes when it opens.
bugs.actual: Opening Trace from the sidebar showed '<N> Goroutines' with no list under it.
reproSteps: Sign in as a site administrator.
Open Site Administration > Monitoring > Trace.
bugs.reason: Intended: routers/web/admin/stacktrace.go deliberately loads no process data until Running Processes or Stacktrace is chosen ('by default, do not do anything which might cause server errors… this page is the entrance of the chance to collect diagnosis report'), so the page stays usable for downloading a diagnosis report when the server is struggling. Both tabs load the list. That the page doesn't tell the administrator how to see traces is a separate accepted bug, gitea-admin-trace-page-hides-how-to-see-traces.

matchingGuidance.scope: Only the claim that the Trace page's empty default list is a loading failure or broken list. Reports that the page doesn't show or explain how to see traces match gitea-admin-trace-page-hides-how-to-see-traces instead.

relatedReference.distinction: That entry is the accepted bug that the page doesn't communicate how to see traces; this entry rejects only the claim that the empty default list is broken.

bugs.name: Monitoring Trace initially shows a count without stack traces
bugs.summary: Opening Monitoring > Trace without a selected trace view shows a goroutine count and no trace bodies.
bugs.expected: The report expects the initial page to select and populate a diagnostic view automatically.
bugs.actual: Selecting Running Processes or Stacktrace populates diagnostics; the unselected landing page is empty.
reproSteps: Open Site Administration > Monitoring > Trace.
Observe the unselected landing view.
Select Running Processes or Stacktrace and compare.
bugs.reason: Intentional landing view: source explicitly avoids collecting trace details until a view is selected and describes the initial page as an entrance for downloading a diagnosis report. This does not cover an explicitly selected diagnostic tab failing to load.

bugs.name: Performance Trace has no administration navigation entry in production
bugs.summary: The Performance Trace endpoint can be opened directly but is absent from administration navigation.
bugs.expected: The report expects a visible navigation entry for the available endpoint.
bugs.actual: Monitoring and Trace tabs omit Performance Trace in production.
reproSteps: Open Site Administration > Monitoring > Trace in production mode.
Inspect the navigation and trace tabs.
Compare with directly opening the Performance Trace endpoint.
bugs.reason: Intentional: source comments explicitly require hiding the Performance Trace tab in production and direct end users to download a diagnosis report instead.

bugs.name: Administrator organization-creation checkbox remains checked after clearing it
bugs.summary: The report says saving an administrator with May Create Organizations unchecked ignores the submitted flag.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that the flag disables an administrator’s organization-creation permission and the checkbox stays unchecked.
bugs.actual: The form shows the effective permission as checked because administrator status independently grants organization creation.
reproSteps: Edit an administrator in Site Administration.
Clear May Create Organizations and save.
Reopen the edit form and compare with a non-administrator.
bugs.reason: The update handler persists the submitted flag, while the form renders CanCreateOrganization, which is always true for administrators. Reject the reported ignored-save/permission-removal claim. This does not settle a separately reported misleading or ineffective control as a GUI-only issue.

matchingGuidance.scope: Claim that the saved flag is ignored or must prevent administrator organization creation; a separately narrowed misleading-control claim is not rejected here.

bugs.name: Queue Remove all submits without an additional confirmation
bugs.summary: The report expects an additional confirmation before the explicitly named queue Remove all action.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is a separate confirmation before submitting removal.
bugs.actual: Clicking Remove all submits the operation immediately. Only an empty queue was tested.
reproSteps: Open Site Administration > Monitoring > Queues.
Open a queue whose item count is zero.
Click Remove all and observe the response.
bugs.reason: Only an empty queue was tested; the named Remove all action submits successfully. No incorrect deletion or established extra-confirmation requirement is demonstrated, so the reported functional bug is unsupported.

bugs.name: Repository deletion links have no accessible name
bugs.summary: Repository deletion links contain only a decorative icon and have no accessible name.
bugs.expected: The link announces its deletion action to assistive technology.
bugs.actual: The operation link is exposed as an unnamed link, although activating it opens the repository deletion confirmation.
reproSteps: Open Site Administration → Repositories.
Inspect the operation link in a repository row using the accessibility tree.
Activate it to identify the deletion action, then cancel the confirmation.

reviewEvidence.basis: User-requested correction after rereading the browser bug-reproducer requirements.
analysis: Pure accessibility: tab order/skips, keyboard-only reachability, focus traps/escape, roles or names and implementation details alone are not benchmark product bugs unless supplied requirements or product documentation explicitly demand that behavior.
Prior acceptance used severity guidance without first checking reproducer eligibility.
limitations: No new browser reproduction is claimed. The correction concerns benchmark eligibility, not whether the application meets general accessibility standards.

bugs.reason: Excluded by the browser bug-reproducer pure-accessibility rule. This report establishes only keyboard/focus/accessibility semantics or a generic contrast threshold, without an explicit supplied product requirement or documented promise for that behavior. Ordinary pointer functionality or visible setting values are not alleged to fail. This negative reference is scoped to the reported accessibility-only claim; it does not cover independently demonstrated data loss, pointer failures, or an explicitly documented keyboard action.

bugs.name: Last Sign-In column sorting cannot be operated by keyboard
bugs.summary: The sortable table headers are plain, non-focusable th elements with click handlers rather than keyboard-operable controls. Last Sign-In is not present in the Sort menu, leaving keyboard users no way to sort by that field.
bugs.expected: Sortable headers are keyboard focusable and operable, or equivalent sorting options are provided in a keyboard-accessible control.
bugs.actual: The header is a plain th with no focusable control or tabindex; sorting by Last Sign-In is available by mouse but not through the Sort menu.
reproSteps: Open Site Administration > User Accounts.
Click the Last Sign-In column header and observe that the URL changes to sort=lastlogin and rows are reordered.
Navigate through the page with Tab and try to focus and activate the Last Sign-In header; it is skipped.
Open the Sort menu and observe that Last Sign-In is not offered there.

bugs.name: Running process cancellation is inaccessible to keyboard users
bugs.summary: The cancel-process control is a non-focusable anchor with no href, tabindex, or accessible name, so it cannot be reached or activated with the keyboard.
bugs.expected: The cancel control is a focusable, named button or link that keyboard and screen-reader users can operate.
bugs.actual: The control is an anchor without an href or tabindex containing only an aria-hidden icon; it cannot receive focus and has no accessible name.

Find the red trash icon next to the current HTTP process; click it to confirm that it opens a Cancel process dialog, then dismiss the dialog.
Try to reach the same icon using Tab, or inspect its markup and accessibility tree.
